title: Reduced singleton stacks over a field have a finite residue-field topological model
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $\mathcal Z$ an algebraic stack over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Use the field-valued point set and smooth-atlas topology of [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open]. Assume that $|\mathcal Z|$ is a singleton, that $\mathcal Z$ is reduced (it admits a reduced smooth scheme atlas, meaning the local rings of that atlas have no nonzero nilpotents), and that $\mathcal Z$ is locally of finite type over $k$ (on smooth scheme charts, in the sense of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). There exist a finite field extension $K/k$, meaning $K$ is finite-dimensional as a $k$-vector space, and a $k$-morphism $\pi:\mathcal Z\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ such that for every algebraic stack $\mathcal T$ and every morphism $\mathcal T\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ the projection induces a homeomorphism $|\mathcal Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\mathcal T|\xrightarrow{\sim}|\mathcal T|$. The product is the 2-fibre product of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. No separation or finiteness condition on the inertia of $\mathcal Z$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 06R6 (lemma-locally-finite-type-locally-noetherian), 06QK (lemma-noetherian-singleton-stack-gerbe), 06QI (lemma-gerbe-fppf), and 06R9 (lemma-gerbe-bijection-points); spaces-descent.tex Tag 06EW (lemma-locally-finite-type-fppf-local-source); decent-spaces.tex Tag 0ACA (lemma-conditions-on-space-over-field), (2) implies (5); spaces-over-fields.tex Tag 06S0 (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-over-field), (1) implies (5).

proof.text: Choose a reduced smooth surjective atlas $u:U\to\mathcal Z$ from the hypotheses. Its composite to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type by the chart meaning of the hypothesis. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $U$ locally Noetherian. Thus $\mathcal Z$ is reduced and locally Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-singleton-gerbe] over $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ to obtain a reduced locally Noetherian singleton algebraic space $Q/k$ and a gerbe $p:\mathcal Z\to Q$ over $k$.

By [lem-sfb-gerbe-smooth-universal-homeomorphism], $pu:U\to Q$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Both $U\to Q$ and $Q\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ are maps of algebraic spaces, hence representable by algebraic spaces as stack maps. Their composite $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type by step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-representable-lft-fppf-source-descent] to these two maps to conclude that $Q\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type. This avoids applying representable descent to the possibly nonrepresentable gerbe map itself.

The singleton space $|Q|$ is discrete: its only subsets are empty and the whole space. By [lem-sfb-space-field-discreteness-criterion], $Q\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally quasi-finite; use its discreteness equivalence, which needs no separatedness. Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-quasifinite-space-field-decomposition] to the reduced space $Q$. In its decomposition $Q\simeq\coprod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Spec}K_i$, every summand has one point. Since $|Q|$ has exactly one point, $I$ has exactly one element. Its field $K$ is finite-dimensional over $k$ and gives a $k$-isomorphism $e:Q\simeq\operatorname{Spec}K$.

Set $\pi=ep$. For any $\mathcal T\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, regard $\mathcal T$ as a stack over $Q$ using $e^{-1}$. The isomorphism $e$ identifies $\mathcal Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\mathcal T$ with $\mathcal Z\times_Q\mathcal T$, compatibly with projection to $\mathcal T$. The universal homeomorphism clause of [lem-sfb-gerbe-smooth-universal-homeomorphism] now gives exactly the required homeomorphism on point spaces. All structure maps are over $k$; no condition on inertia was introduced.
